title: Classes and Objects
description: Defining your own types: classes, objects and constructors, access modifiers and encapsulation; the F10 Project 1 brief that models a real-world object, handles null and builds with Maven dependencies; then what a reference really is: stack versus heap, string immutability, == versus equals, final and toString, and enums.
sourceCoverageNotes: Course slice: Foundation days F4-F18 (curriculum/snapshot/pep-curriculum.json /tracks/0/weeks/0/days/3 to /tracks/0/weeks/3/days/2). This module covers F9, F10, F11 (/tracks/0/weeks/1/days/3, /tracks/0/weeks/1/days/4, /tracks/0/weeks/2/days/0).
Module grouping is a second-mate grouping decision recorded at intake (matrix record source-gap-java-foundations-modules), not syllabus: modules follow calendar day order and hold 4-9 topics.
Every calendar row of these days maps to exactly one topic or project brief with relation exact; there are no splits or shared rows.

F10 is a Project day: its three rows map to one canonical, reusable learner-facing project brief, classes-in-practice-project (kind lab-brief, because the topic schema has no project kind), whose topic coding lab holds one starter scaffold and one public test suite, test command mvn -q -o test. It is not a syllabus topic; topicOrder places it in calendar order. Standard and Fast overlays reference this same artifact (captain decision pep-project-rows, option A; intake-2 reconciliation education-recheck-01 and -02).
